section_summary: This section records the 1930 visits of the Japanese vessels Hakuyo Maru and Hakuho Maru to Alaskan waters, alongside reports of Japanese fishing and other vessel activity in the Bering Sea. The 1933 correspondence centers on proposed cruises by both ships, requests for port courtesies, and disagreement over access to the Aleutian and Pribilof Islands. State, Navy, Commerce, and other officials weigh strategic concerns against cooperation on fur-seal protection before offering access to staffed ports and a Coast Guard escort for the Hakuho Maru.

subfiles.title: Governor Parks's radiogram and Interior referral
subfiles.from: George Parks; Department of the Interior
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary Edwards; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Alaskan officials were instructed to observe and report on the Japanese vessel.
subfiles.summary: Parks says customs, marshal, and Bering Sea Patrol officials will report after gathering information.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Hakuho Maru patrol reporting
subfiles.about: State expects Treasury to receive reports on the Hakuho Maru's movements.
subfiles.summary: State notes that Treasury and Interior were notified of the planned Alaskan cruise and expects the Bering Sea Patrol to report observations.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japanese request for Hakuho Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: U.S. authorities have been instructed to extend customary courtesies if the Hakuho Maru calls at Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: The note acknowledges the seal-observation cruise and confirms that appropriate authorities have issued instructions for the ship's reception.

subfiles.title: Japanese reply on Pribilof observers
subfiles.about: Japan will send no observer to the Pribilof fur-seal industry that year.
subfiles.summary: The reply distinguishes the observer inquiry from the Hakuyo Maru's visit.

subfiles.title: Commerce inquiry about Japanese Pribilof observer
subfiles.about: Commerce asks whether Japan plans to send a fur-seal observer so quarters can be arranged.
subfiles.summary: Commerce seeks advance notice of any Japanese representative.

subfiles.title: State reply on absence of Japanese Pribilof observer
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Japan will send no Pribilof observer, a response separate from the Hakuyo Maru cruise.
subfiles.summary: Carr relays the Japanese Embassy's negative verbal answer.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard memorandum on Hakuyo Maru arrival
subfiles.from: F. C. Billard, Coast Guard Commandant
subfiles.about: The Hakuyo Maru arrived at Dutch Harbor and received customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: A patrol despatch gives the arrival, complement, and intended onward route.

subfiles.title: Governor Parks's report on Hakuyo Maru reception
subfiles.about: Alaskan officials extended courtesies to the Hakuyo Maru after its Dutch Harbor arrival.
subfiles.summary: Parks quotes earlier instructions and a patrol report, and promises to forward the customs collector's written account.

subfiles.title: Commerce report on Hakuyo Maru at St. Paul
subfiles.about: The Hakuyo Maru's students visited a St. Paul seal rookery.
subfiles.summary: Quoting Superintendent Christoffers, Commerce reports the July visit, explains the ship's training role, and distinguishes it from the Hakuho Maru.

subfiles.title: Commerce report on Hakuho Maru and other Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Commerce relays sightings of the Hakuho Maru, a Japanese warship, and the crab-fishing Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Christoffers quotes reports from Attu and Amatignak, including unverified suspicions about sea otters and observations of worn landing boats. The Hakuyo Maru reportedly canned crabs in Bristol Bay.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Commerce vessel reports to Tokyo
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: State forwards three Commerce reports on Japanese fishing vessels off Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Copies of letters dated August 13, 16, and 19 are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Commerce report on Taihoyu floating cannery
subfiles.about: A Coast Guard telegram reports the Taihoyu and launches catching and canning crabs offshore.
subfiles.summary: Commerce passes along the patrol's August 14 sighting and position.

subfiles.title: Commerce report on Japanese trawler
subfiles.about: The cutter Chelan observed a Japanese steam trawler fishing 25 miles offshore.
subfiles.summary: Commerce provides the trawler's reported position and promises further reports.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese trawler report to Tokyo
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: State forwards Commerce's August 27 report on a Japanese fishing vessel.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses the trawler sighting for the mission's information.

subfiles.title: Consul General Garrels's report on Hakuyo Maru itinerary
subfiles.about: The Hakuyo Maru plans a 1933 training cruise with calls at American ports.
subfiles.summary: Garrels relays proposed stops and dates, notes a request for free consular services, and suggests notifying port authorities.

subfiles.title: Schedule of proposed Hakuyo Maru American port visits
subfiles.about: A schedule lists the Hakuyo Maru's proposed U.S. port calls.
subfiles.summary: It lists Dutch Harbor, St. Paul, San Francisco, San Pedro, and Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum urging reconsideration of Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.about: State staff recommend reconsidering the refusal of Hakuyo Maru visits to staffed Alaskan ports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum contrasts Navy's earlier objection with its later acceptance of calls where American officials are present. It identifies Unalaska, St. Paul, and St. George as such ports and proposes telling Japan that the visits are now convenient.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ambassador's request for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: Japan seeks customary courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru's planned Pacific cruise.
subfiles.summary: The note names Captain Jinzo Nakagawa and gives the crew, students, and proposed ports.

subfiles.title: Record of delivery of informal reply
subfiles.about: Mr. Hamilton delivered State's informal Hakuyo Maru reply to Mr. Midzusawa.
subfiles.summary: Midzusawa compared it jokingly with Japan's restrictions on U.S. naval visits.

subfiles.title: Informal memorandum restricting Hakuyo Maru's port calls
subfiles.about: State welcomes the Hakuyo Maru at mainland and Hawaiian ports but asks it to omit Alaskan island calls.
subfiles.summary: The stated reason is difficulty arranging an adequate reception at the other ports.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo on Hakuyo Maru reply
subfiles.about: State informs the embassy of its informal reply restricting Hakuyo Maru port calls.
subfiles.summary: The telegram quotes the request to omit visits to the Alaskan island ports.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of May 6 telegram, first copy
subfiles.about: A paraphrase records State's reply on Hakuyo Maru port access.
subfiles.summary: It repeats the welcome at mainland and Hawaiian ports and request to omit other calls.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of May 6 telegram, second copy
subfiles.about: A second paraphrase records the same Hakuyo Maru communication.
subfiles.summary: It duplicates the substance of the preceding paraphrase.

subfiles.title: Payments under the North Pacific Sealing Convention
subfiles.about: A table lists U.S. payments to Britain or Canada and Japan under the 1911 sealing convention.
subfiles.summary: It gives fiscal-year amounts, totals, and an explanatory note about advance payments.

subfiles.title: Request to California for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru's California calls.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to Agriculture for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to Interior for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to Labor for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to Navy for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to Treasury for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: Request to War for Hakuyo Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State requests usual courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the itinerary and ship's complement.

subfiles.title: War Department reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Army commanders have been told to extend customary courtesies to the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Instructions went to the Ninth Corps Area and Hawaiian Department.

subfiles.title: Treasury Department reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.from: W. W. Roluf, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Customs collectors at the mainland and Hawaiian ports are authorized to assist the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Treasury names San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Honolulu customs offices.

subfiles.title: California Governor's Office reply
subfiles.from: Private Secretary to Governor James Rolph Jr.
subfiles.about: California will ask harbor officials to extend courtesies to the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The private secretary replies on Governor Rolph's behalf.

subfiles.title: Policy memorandum on Japanese access to Alaskan ports
subfiles.about: A State official argues against linking Hakuyo Maru port access to U.S. naval access to Japanese mandated islands.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews earlier policy, legal concerns, and the diplomatic cost of refusing a Japanese vessel access to normally open American ports. It recommends informal discussion with Navy rather than using this cruise to press the broader dispute.

subfiles.title: Navy Department objection to Alaskan island calls
subfiles.about: Navy accepts mainland and Honolulu calls but objects to visits where no U.S. officials are present.
subfiles.summary: Navy invokes Japan's similar position on visits to mandated islands and asks State to discourage calls at unstaffed Aleutian ports.

subfiles.title: Labor Department reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Immigration officers have been asked to treat the Hakuyo Maru's passengers courteously.
subfiles.summary: Their courtesies remain subject to immigration law.

subfiles.title: Governor Troy's radiogram and Interior referral
subfiles.from: John W. Troy; Department of the Interior
subfiles.to: John H. Edwards; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Alaska raises no objection to the Hakuyo Maru's fishery studies and offers assistance.
subfiles.summary: Troy suggests consulting the Bureau of Fisheries.

subfiles.title: Governor Judd's radiogram and Interior referral
subfiles.from: Governor Judd; Department of the Interior
subfiles.to: Department of the Interior; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hawaii has no objection to the Hakuyo Maru's Honolulu visit.
subfiles.summary: Judd promises the usual courtesies and facilities.

subfiles.title: Navy clarification on staffed Alaskan ports
subfiles.about: Navy withdraws its objection to Hakuyo Maru visits at Dutch Harbor, St. Paul, and St. George.
subfiles.summary: Lammers explains that Navy's earlier objection concerned ports without suitable American officials.

subfiles.title: Japanese consul's request to Bureau of Fisheries
subfiles.about: The Japanese consul requests assistance for Hakuyo Maru visits to Dutch Harbor and St. Paul.
subfiles.summary: He describes the ship, complement, training purpose, proposed landing dates, and need for courtesies and emergency help.

subfiles.title: Tentative itinerary of Hakuyo Maru's eighth cruise
subfiles.about: A detailed schedule traces the Hakuyo Maru's Pacific training cruise.
subfiles.summary: The table lists ports, arrival and departure dates, distances, fishing areas, and the cruise's instructional purpose.

subfiles.title: Salisbury's guidance to Bower on Japanese consul's request
subfiles.about: Salisbury suggests how to answer the consul's request for Hakuyo Maru calls in Alaska.
subfiles.summary: He recounts State's May 6 request that the ship omit Dutch Harbor and Pribilof visits, while welcoming mainland and Hawaiian calls.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Navy on Hakuyo Maru's proposed visits
subfiles.about: State and Navy officials discuss whether to refuse Hakuyo Maru access to Aleutian and Pribilof ports.
subfiles.summary: Lammers cites reciprocal treatment and fears of strategic surveys. Hornbeck questions the proposed explanation and warns of diplomatic costs, but Navy subsequently maintains its objection.

subfiles.title: State memorandum on Hakuho Maru access and fur-seal cooperation
subfiles.about: Officials weigh Navy's proposed limits on Hakuho Maru port calls against fur-seal treaty obligations.
subfiles.summary: Navy favors access only to staffed ports, chiefly Unalaska, while Commerce fears that restriction could damage Japanese cooperation on fur seals and fisheries. The memorandum proposes a State, Navy, and Commerce conference before replying.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ambassador's request for Hakuho Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: Japan seeks facilities if the Hakuho Maru needs shelter or provisions in the Aleutians.
subfiles.summary: The note describes Captain Eiichi Taketomi's planned fur-seal and anti-poaching cruise.

subfiles.title: Record of clarification to Japanese Embassy
subfiles.about: Salisbury explains why State's note named fewer ports for the Hakuho Maru than for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: He says the Hakuho Maru request covered only the Aleutians and expects Pribilof permission if requested.

subfiles.title: Recommendation for Coast Guard escort of Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State, Navy, and Commerce officials favor assigning a Coast Guard cutter to accompany the Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.summary: An escort would permit assistance at otherwise unstaffed Aleutian ports while addressing Navy's concerns and Commerce's fears for fur-seal and salmon interests. The memorandum reports Coast Guard readiness and support for reopening the Hakuyo Maru case.

subfiles.title: State reply granting staffed-port access and offering escort
subfiles.about: State offers a Coast Guard escort for the Hakuho Maru and permits the Hakuyo Maru to call at staffed Alaskan ports.
subfiles.summary: The Hakuho Maru may receive customary courtesies at Unalaska; a cutter could assist it at other Aleutian ports if Japan supplies meeting details. State also reverses its earlier position on Hakuyo Maru calls at Unalaska, St. Paul, and St. George.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Interior on Hakuho Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State asks Interior to extend courtesies at Aleutian ports where its officials are stationed.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses Japan's May 9 request and asks Interior to report its action.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Treasury on Hakuho Maru courtesies
subfiles.about: State asks Treasury to extend courtesies at Aleutian ports where its officials are stationed.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses Japan's May 9 request and asks Treasury to report its action.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo on revised Japanese vessel access
subfiles.about: State informs the embassy of its revised arrangements for both Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The telegram quotes the offer of courtesies at Unalaska and a Coast Guard escort for the Hakuho Maru. It also reports that the Hakuyo Maru may visit Unalaska, St. Paul, and St. George.

subfiles.title: Commerce consultation on Hakuho Maru request
subfiles.about: State asks whether Commerce objects to Japan's request for Hakuho Maru courtesies.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses the Ambassador's May 9 note.

subfiles.title: Navy consultation on Hakuho Maru request
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State asks whether Navy objects to Hakuho Maru calls for shelter or provisions.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses the Ambassador's May 9 note and describes the proposed Aleutian fur-seal cruise.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on treaty risks of refusing Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: State assesses how refusing Hakuho Maru port access could affect fur-seal and salmon interests.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum warns that Japan might use refusal to justify denouncing the 1911 Fur Seal Treaty, removing a possible bargaining point on Japanese salmon fishing. It cites Article VIII's cooperation clause and recalls reports that earlier Hakuho Maru cruises disturbed Aleutian residents.
